title: Minimal change nephropathy
diseaseDescription: Bounded human minimal change nephropathy observations: nephrin-reactive antibodies, immune-cell and urinary IL-8 associations, foot-process effacement and nephrotic presentation. Not a complete causal circuit or comprehensive literature synthesis. Secondary causes and FSGS are not modeled; the effacement case has an infection-associated course.
releaseNote: Overall scientific summary of minimal-change-nephropathy-candidate-ea826765a33b; external current-literature review remains pending. View-only edit of minimal-change-nephropathy-summary-candidate-bc5dfdb78dfb (5af3dd6be089e6f2fc406703c21d046fbcbae59f7040d389c4c559d7698616f6): the default map is a layered human-evidence view (immune findings, anti-nephrin and nephrotic-syndrome hubs, podocyte and clinical outcomes); the experimental anti-nephrin/IL-13 view is relabelled and laid out without edges crossing nodes; the redundant research view is removed. Scientific records are unchanged; domain review pending.

claims.text: Circulating nephrin autoantibodies were identified in a subset of adults and children with active MCD using nephrin-specific assays.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Subset-specific observation, not proof of antibody-mediated injury in every patient.

claims.text: Circulating nephrin autoantibodies correlated with podocyte-associated punctate IgG in institutional renal biopsies.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Colocalization and correlation do not establish causal sufficiency.

claims.text: Anti-nephrin-positive patients had a larger plasmablast fraction at diagnosis, but the between-group difference was not statistically significant.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Small cohort; a nonsignificant difference does not demonstrate antibody production by a particular B-cell subset.

claims.text: An adult with nephrotic syndrome had biopsy findings consistent with MCD, including diffuse foot-process effacement, followed by spontaneous proteinuria resolution.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Single infection-associated case; temporal observations do not establish direction or generality.
Reclassified as clinical natural-history context (spontaneous remission and relapse); it does not identify an initiating mechanism.

claims.text: An adult with biopsy-confirmed MCD presented with nephrotic-range proteinuria of 8.64 g/day and hypoalbuminemia.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Single adult case with hypertension and prediabetes; no population-wide estimate.

claims.text: Urinary IL-8 was increased during relapse compared with remission or controls in children with biopsy-proven MCD.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Cached abstract is truncated at the results p-value; no numerical significance threshold is inferred.

claims.text: The authors concluded that IL-8 and TNF-alpha may not play a disease-specific pathogenic role, qualifying a causal reading of the urinary IL-8 association.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Full assay results are unavailable in the truncated abstract; no detailed negative mechanism is asserted.
The negative albumin-permeability finding applies to the tested conditions; it does not exclude context-dependent cytokine effects.

claims.text: Peripheral CD4 T-cell expansion and increased CD69 activation coincided with MCD onset.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Association only; bulk leukocyte expression does not establish a cell-specific permeability-factor pathway.
A human association only; not an established initiating cause, permeability-factor source or necessary disease mechanism.

claims.text: Anti-nephrin autoantibodies were detected in 50% of 60 MCD patients and 70% of those in active phase; levels correlated positively with proteinuria and inversely with serum albumin.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Cross-sectional correlations; assay-dependent prevalence.

claims.text: Anti-nephrin-positive MCD patients had a predominant IgG4 subclass with elevated serum IL-4 and IL-13 and an increased IL-4/IFN-gamma ratio, consistent with Th2 skewing.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Cross-sectional association; does not show that Th2 cytokines drive antibody production or podocyte injury.
Small single-disease sample; links humoral and Th2 findings without establishing their sequence.

claims.text: In 596 biopsy-diagnosed adult Chinese patients with MCD or primary FSGS, anti-nephrin antibodies fell during clinical remission and reappeared before proteinuria relapse.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Mixed MCD and primary FSGS cohort; MCD-specific longitudinal estimates are not separated in the abstract.
Different assay (ELISA, including IgM) from the multicentre immunoprecipitation-based cohort; prevalence is assay-dependent.

claims.text: Passive transfer of IgG from an anti-nephrin-positive MCD patient to a rabbit caused proteinuria and podocyte foot-process effacement without electron-dense deposits, absent in the control rabbit.
limitations: IgG from a single patient was transferred to one rabbit, with one control rabbit; total IgG rather than purified nephrin-specific IgG was transferred.
Experimental induction in rabbits does not establish the mechanism in every human case or in antibody-negative disease.
Supplementary figures not inspected; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: Patient-derived anti-nephrin IgG bound glomerular nephrin and strongly increased nephrin tyrosine phosphorylation in the recipient rabbit.
limitations: IgG from a single patient was transferred to one rabbit, with one control rabbit; total IgG rather than purified nephrin-specific IgG was transferred.
Experimental induction in rabbits does not establish the mechanism in every human case or in antibody-negative disease.
Supplementary figures not inspected; independent domain review pending.
The downstream sequence from phosphorylation to cytoskeletal change and effacement was not established.

claims.text: In 17 therapy-naive adults with biopsy-proven MCD, 12 were anti-nephrin positive; all 12 reached complete remission with undetectable antibodies after 8 weeks of steroids.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Small uncontrolled cohort; antibody clearance and remission are concurrent and do not show that antibody reduction alone explains treatment benefit.
The authors’ statement that this explains the steroid response is not adopted as a causal claim.

claims.text: Anti-nephrin autoantibody levels correlated with disease activity at inclusion and during follow-up.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Correlation with activity does not by itself establish pathogenicity in humans.

claims.text: Active immunization of mice with recombinant nephrin induced nephrotic syndrome with an MCD-like phenotype, IgG at the slit diaphragm, nephrin phosphorylation and severe podocyte cytoskeletal changes.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Experimental sufficiency in mice; does not establish the mechanism or its prevalence in every human case.
Active immunization with murine nephrin differs from spontaneous human autoimmunity.

claims.text: In a multicentre cohort, anti-nephrin autoantibodies were detected in 46 of 105 adults (44%) with MCD, rising to 69% in active MCD without immunosuppressive treatment.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Prevalence is cohort- and assay-dependent; the overall adult MCD figure (46/105, 44%) is lower than the active untreated subgroup.
Antibody-negative MCD is not explained by this finding.

claims.text: IL-13 overexpression in rats produced albuminuria, hypoalbuminemia and up to 80% podocyte foot-process fusion without significant light-microscopic glomerular change.
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Experimental sufficiency of IL-13 overexpression in rats; does not establish that IL-13 is necessary or independently causal in human MCD.

claims.text: IL-13 overexpression in rats downregulated glomerular nephrin, podocin and dystroglycan and upregulated B7-1 (CD80).
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Experimental sufficiency of IL-13 overexpression in rats; does not establish that IL-13 is necessary or independently causal in human MCD.
Expression changes do not establish whether nephrin loss is upstream of effacement in this model.

mapViews.label: Human evidence · immune findings to podocyte injury

scientificSummary.scope: A bounded podocyte-injury circuit of primary minimal change nephropathy: circulating factors and T-cell activity, foot-process effacement and nephrotic syndrome. Excludes secondary causes and other glomerulopathies.

paragraphs.text: In 17 therapy-naive adults with biopsy-proven MCD, 12 were anti-nephrin positive; all 12 reached complete remission with undetectable antibodies after 8 weeks of steroids. Peripheral CD4 T-cell expansion and increased CD69 activation coincided with MCD onset. An adult with nephrotic syndrome had biopsy findings consistent with MCD, including diffuse foot-process effacement, followed by spontaneous proteinuria resolution.

These selected findings describe a bounded candidate, whose overall explanation has not been independently checked against current literature. Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending. Small uncontrolled cohort; antibody clearance and remission are concurrent and do not show that antibody reduction alone explains treatment benefit. Treatment efficacy has not been synthesized in this summary.
